title: Local quasi-finiteness of schemes is etale local on the source
statement: Let $U,V,T$ be schemes [def-pc-scheme], let $p:U\to V$ be etale [def-weil-etale-morphism], and let $g:V\to T$ be a morphism. If $g$ is locally quasi-finite in the scheme sense [pqf-def-quasifinite], then $g\circ p$ is locally quasi-finite. Conversely, if the underlying map of points of $p$ is surjective and $g\circ p$ is locally quasi-finite, then $g$ is locally quasi-finite. No quasi-compactness, separatedness or Noetherian hypothesis is imposed on these schemes or morphisms.

source.place: Tag 03X4 (lemma-locally-quasi-finite-etale-local-source), including the etale-precomposition assertion in its proof; source locality means the covering equivalence of definition-property-morphisms-local-source.

proof.text: Open restrictions of the etale map $p$ remain etale: let $A\subseteq U$, $B\subseteq V$ be opens with $p(A)\subseteq B$, and $x\in A$. Flatness at $x$ is unchanged, since the local-ring map $\mathcal O_{V,p(x)}\to\mathcal O_{U,x}$ is the same for $A\to B$. For local finite presentation, [def-sbc-locally-finite-presentation] for $p$ gives affine opens $x\in U'=\operatorname{Spec}A'$, $V'=\operatorname{Spec}R$ with $p(U')\subseteq V'$ and $R\to A'$ of finite presentation. Choose $r\in R$ with $p(x)\in D(r)\subseteq V'\cap B$ and $a\in A'$ with $x\in D(a)\subseteq U'\cap A\cap p^{-1}(D(r))$. Then $A'_a\cong A'[t]/(at-1)$ is finitely presented over $R$; the image of $r$ is a unit in $A'_a$, so $A'_a=A'_a\otimes_RR_r$ is the base change of $R\to A'_a$ along $R\to R_r$, hence finitely presented over $R_r$. These affine opens $D(a)\subseteq A$, $D(r)\subseteq B$ witness finite presentation of $A\to B$ at $x$; a finite presentation has finitely many generators, so $A\to B$ is also locally of finite type. The diagonal of $A\to B$ is the restriction of the diagonal of $p$ to the open $A\times_B A=A\times_VA\subseteq U\times_VU$, so it is an open immersion [def-weil-open-immersion]. Thus [def-weil-unramified-morphism] and [def-weil-etale-morphism] apply to $A\to B$. In particular $p^{-1}(B)\to B$ is etale; if $p$ is surjective it is surjective on points, since a preimage of a point of $B$ automatically belongs to $p^{-1}(B)$.

source.place: Tag 02GI (definition-etale), open restriction; the point-local definitions and restricted diagonal give the argument explicitly.

proof.text: Suppose $g$ is locally quasi-finite and fix $u\in U$. Choose an affine open $Z\subseteq T$ containing $g(p(u))$, an affine open $W\subseteq g^{-1}(Z)$ containing $p(u)$, and an affine open $A\subseteq p^{-1}(W)$ containing $u$. By [lem-a1-scheme-lqf-affine-criterion], the ring map $\mathcal O_T(Z)\to\mathcal O_V(W)$ is of finite type and quasi-finite at every target prime. By Step 1, $A\to W$ is etale, so [lem-weil-pbc-etale-ring-map-quasi-finite] gives the same two properties for $\mathcal O_V(W)\to\mathcal O_U(A)$. Apply [lem-trf-quasi-finite-composition] to these two ring maps. Functoriality of structure-sheaf pullback identifies their composite with the map for $A\to Z$. It is therefore of finite type and quasi-finite at the prime representing $u$. These affine neighbourhoods witness quasi-finiteness of $g\circ p$ at $u$ in [pqf-def-quasifinite]; doing this at every $u$ proves the first assertion.

source.place: Tag 03X4, precomposition paragraph; its ring-map composition argument is Tag 00PO, using the affine characterization Tag 01TK.

proof.text: For the converse assume $p$ is surjective and $g\circ p$ is locally quasi-finite. By [lem-weil-pbc-lqf-locally-finite-type], $g\circ p$ is locally of finite type. The definition [def-weil-etale-morphism] supplies flatness and local finite presentation of $p$. Hence [lem-a1-lft-flat-lfp-source-descent], applied to the triangle $U\xrightarrow{p}V\xrightarrow{g}T$, shows that $g$ is locally of finite type. This use does not require $p$ to be quasi-compact.

source.place: Tag 03X4, finite-type descent; Tag 02KL (lemma-flat-finitely-presented-permanence), locally-of-finite-type alternative, packages the same Tag 0367 affine descent and finite affine refinement for non-affine source covers.

proof.text: Fix an affine open $Z\subseteq T$ and an affine open $W\subseteq V$ with $g(W)\subseteq Z$. Step 1 gives a surjective etale map $p^{-1}(W)\to W$. Apply [lem-weil-pbc-etale-covering-affine-refinement] to this singleton covering of the affine scheme $W$. Obtain finitely many affine open subschemes $A_1,\ldots,A_m\subseteq p^{-1}(W)$ whose images under $p$ cover $W$. Each $A_j$ is also an open subscheme of $U$. By [lem-weil-pbc-lqf-restriction-to-opens], $A_j\to Z$, the restriction of $g\circ p$, is locally quasi-finite.

source.place: Tag 03X4, affine reduction expanded using Topologies Tag 0218 (lemma-etale-affine); Morphisms Tag 01TK, restriction to opens.

proof.text: For each $j$, both $A_j$ and $Z$ are affine, so [lem-weil-pbc-morphism-affine-schemes-affine] says that $A_j\to Z$ is affine; [lem-weil-pbc-affine-morphism-permanence], clause (3), makes it quasi-compact. With its local quasi-finiteness from Step 4, [pqf-lem-qf-locqf-qc] implies that $A_j\to Z$ is quasi-finite. By [pqf-lem-qf-finitefibres], every set $(g\circ p)|_{A_j}^{-1}(t)$, for $t\in Z$, is finite.

source.place: Tag 03X4, finite-fibres paragraph; Morphisms Tags 01SH, 01S7, 02NH and lemma-quasi-finite-locally-quasi-compact.

proof.text: For $t\in Z$, the set $\{w\in W:g(w)=t\}$ is the union, over $1\le j\le m$, of the images under $p$ of $\{a\in A_j:g(p(a))=t\}$. Indeed, the image is contained in that set, and conversely the covering of $W$ by the $p(A_j)$ supplies a preimage of every such $w$, which necessarily maps to $t$. Each source set is finite by Step 5, so its image is finite and the finite union is finite. Thus $W\to Z$ has finite fibres. The same argument covers $m=0$: then $W$ is empty and every fibre is empty.

source.place: Tag 03X4, finite fibres descend through the surjection; the finite affine refinement replaces its single affine source.

proof.text: The restriction $g|_W:W\to Z$ is locally of finite type: [lem-weil-pbc-lft-affine-pairs] for $g$ from Step 3 gives the finite-type ring map for every pair of affine opens inside $W,Z$, so the reverse direction of that criterion applies to $g|_W$. Since $W,Z$ are affine, [lem-weil-pbc-morphism-affine-schemes-affine] and [lem-weil-pbc-affine-morphism-permanence](3) also make $g|_W$ quasi-compact. It is of finite type by [def-weil-finite-type-morphism]. Now [pqf-lem-qf-finitefibres], using Step 6, makes $g|_W$ quasi-finite, and [pqf-lem-qf-locqf-qc] makes it locally quasi-finite. Take an affine open cover of $T$ and, over each member $Z$, an affine open cover by such $W$ of $g^{-1}(Z)$. Condition (3) of [lem-a1-scheme-lqf-affine-criterion] proves that $g$ is locally quasi-finite. All finiteness was used only on these affine charts, so there is no global quasi-compactness or separation requirement.

split_report.summary: Expanded Stacks 03X4 into seven steps. Proved etale precomposition on affine charts using the existing ring composition theorem. For descent, descend local finite type, refine over each affine source chart by finitely many affine etale pieces, descend finite fibres as finite images, and glue. Created only the general 01TK affine criterion and 02KL local finite-type source descent, both statement-only unsplit nodes; reused all existing finite-fibre and affine-permanence results. Statement unchanged.
